world.bio: Cabinetmaker for twenty years, running my own one-man workshop in a rented shed in Brunswick. I build kitchens, built-ins and the odd bit of furniture for architects and private clients, and I still hand-cut dovetails on drawers nobody will ever look at. Separated from my wife, but we share the kids; I coach my daughter's under-12 netball team on Saturdays and I'm slowly restoring a 1978 Holden Kingswood in the driveway of my mum's place in Coburg.
skills_assets: Twenty years of cabinetmaking, mostly kitchens and joinery for architects in the inner north
A 3.2 metre sliding table saw (Felder), a 520mm jointer-planer, a thicknesser, an edgebander and a small CNC router I never got the hang of
A shed in Brunswick, 140 square metres, with three-phase power and a spray booth I share with no one
A Hilux ute with a tray, and a trailer for sheet goods
Relationships with two hardwood yards in Sunshine and Thomastown
A 1978 Holden Kingswood, three years into a restoration, bare shell, matching numbers engine in boxes

projects.name: Hartley kitchen job
projects.text: A big spotted gum kitchen for an architect in Northcote. Eleven cabinets, a 2.8 metre island with a thick top, and a pantry with drawers all dovetailed. Eight weeks of work booked, five done. Clients are lovely but changed the handle spec twice. I have to deliver by 24 October or the architect's schedule collapses. The island top is glued up and waiting for flattening.

projects.name: Kingswood restoration
projects.text: I bought the shell from a bloke in Ballarat for $4,500 three years ago. Body is stripped and primed. The engine is in boxes on pallets in my mum's garage. I only get to it on Sunday mornings, maybe once every two weeks, and every month there's something else: a rear axle, a bad gearbox, a rusty floor pan. The plan was to have it on the road for my 50th. That's in 2028. We'll see.

projects.name: Netball under-12s
projects.text: Training Tuesdays at six at the Brunswick rec centre and games Saturday mornings. We're 3 and 2 this season. My daughter Mia is wing attack and plays like her mother, which is to say ruthlessly.

notes.text: Got the letter from the landlord. Lease on the Brunswick shed went up again. Another jump. January it was $3,800 a month, now $5,300. Forty per cent, give or take. Landlord's agent used the phrase 'market adjustment' about nine times. Standing in the shed with the letter and the smell of cut spotted gum I nearly laughed.

Put a photo of the shed on my business Instagram with the caption: 'Lease on the Brunswick shed went up again.' Eleven likes, one from a bloke who sells timber, one from my sister. A guy from another workshop commented 'Same here mate, mine too'. That's the whole Brunswick manufacturing sector, vented in one comment thread.

Rang a few agents about other sheds. Everything in Brunswick and Coburg is either gone or double. Heard of a place in Dandenong for less but that's an hour each way, and my clients are all inner north. Mia has netball Saturday, I can't be in Dandenong.

Looked up what the Felder is worth second hand. 3.2 metre sliding table saw, I paid $28,000 for it nine years ago and it still cuts like a dream. A guy in Sydney sells the same model for $19,000. The jointer I could get maybe $4,000 for. I priced it just to see. Felt sick doing it. That saw is my twenties and thirties.

Kingswood Sunday. Spent three hours trying to free a seized bolt on the rear subframe. Used heat, penetrating oil, a four-foot breaker bar, swearing. Bolt won. Came home covered in grease and my daughter said 'you smell like a truck'.
Trying to cut back on coffee. Day four. Headache like a bad plane landing. Replaced the second flat white with a green tea and could barely look at it.

Told my ex-wife Jess about the rent over the phone, only because it affects the kid money. She said 'what are you going to do'. I said 'I don't know'. She said 'you've said that before, and you figured it out'. Which is the nicest thing she's said to me in a year.

Hartley kitchen: island glue-up is perfect, but I'm worried about the pantry drawers, the client changed the soft-close to a different brand and the cutouts don't match. Had to rework four drawer fronts. Another half day I didn't plan for.

Coaching: lost 18 to 22. Girls were upset. I told them the score is a number, the thing that matters is whether we passed the ball on the second phase. Mia rolled her eyes. She said Dad, we want to win. Honest, at least.
Walked past a Bunnings and a bloke was trying to carry a sheet of ply on his own. Helped him. He said 'you a chippie?' I said 'cabinetmaker'. He said 'same thing'. It's not, but I let it go.
Mum asked when the Kingswood would be done, she wants the garage back. I said soon. She said you've been saying 'soon' since Dad died. Which is fair.

Bank rang about the equipment loan. They want a refinance meeting. The repayments on the CNC (which I barely use) are more than I'd like. I should've sold that first. Will bring it up with the bloke at the meeting.

messages.text:
Tim: Hi Declan, just confirming the lease renewal at $5,300 per month effective 1 January.
Declan: That's a 40% increase. Is there any flexibility?
Tim: The owner has had the property revalued. Rents in the area are at market.
Declan: I'll think about it.

Jess: Mia needs new netball shoes. Size 5.
Declan: I'll send $90.
Jess: Thanks. You OK? You sound flat.
Declan: Rent.
Jess: Ah.

Priya: Hi Declan, how's the island going?
Declan: Top is glued up, flattening Monday.
Priya: Great. Can we move delivery to the 24th?
Declan: Yep. That's the plan.
Priya: Brilliant. You're a legend.

Gaz: Mate, you still got your saw?
Declan: Why?
Gaz: Bloke I know is after one. Sliding table, 3 metre.
Declan: Not for sale. Maybe.
Gaz: Maybe's good enough for me.

Mum: Dinner Sunday? Roast.
Declan: Sure. I'll bring the kids.
Mum: Bring yourself too. You look thin.

relations.about: Ex-wife, co-parents Mia and Oscar; civil
Son, 8, builds Lego like a draftsman
Lives in Coburg, her garage has my Kingswood engine

constraints: Won't work weekends except Kingswood Sunday
Can't leave inner north: kids and clients
Won't take shortcuts on drawer construction
Doesn't want an employee for now
sensitive: Rent up 40% from January, I priced the saw and jointer for sale
